predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Singhasari'; Jayakatwang's restored Kediri (1292-1293) held the land between.

land.text: Jayakatwang's Kediri, overthrown by the Yuan expedition and Raden Wijaya in 1293

predecessors.note: Per the kediri-kingdom dossier; the Majapahit page does not name Jayakatwang.

the east of East Java, Blambangan

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Blambangan Kingdom'; Cliopatria's row begins 1519.

land.text: Bali: courtiers and priests 'fled east to Bali'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Balinese Kingdom begins 1519; the Majapahit page has the refugees of 1527.

capitals.name: Majapahit (Trowulan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Majapahit (Trowulan)'; Kertabhumi held Trowulan from 1468 until 1478.

capitals.name: Daha (Kediri)
capitals.note: 'moved the kingdom's capital further inland to Daha' after Kertabhumi's rebellion of 1468.

rulers.name: Hayam Wuruk
rulers.note: Infobox: 1350s-1389/1399; the text puts his death in 1389.

rulers.name: Kertawijaya
rulers.note: 'In 1447, Suhita died and was succeeded by Kertawijaya, her brother. He ruled until 1451.'

rulers.name: Rajasawardhana (Bhre Pamotan)
rulers.note: 'After Kertawijaya died, Bhre Pamotan became a king with formal name Rajasawardhana. He died in 1453.' The start year is Kertawijaya's death; the page gives no accession year.

rulers.name: Girisawardhana
rulers.note: 'A three-year kingless period was possibly the result of a succession crisis. Girisawardhana, son of Kertawijaya, came to power in 1456. He died in 1466.' The page spells the name Girisawardhana.

rulers.name: Singhawikramawardhana
rulers.note: 'He died in 1466 and was succeeded by Singhawikramawardhana', who 'continued his rule until he was succeeded by his son Girindrawardhana (Ranawijaya) in 1474'. In 1468 Prince Kertabhumi rebelled and ruled at Trowulan as a rival king to 1478 (see the ledger contest).

rulers.name: Girindrawardhana (Ranawijaya)
rulers.note: The text: 'succeeded by his son Girindrawardhana (Ranawijaya) in 1474' and deposed in 1498 by Udara; the infobox says c. 1486-1527. Reigns 1429-1474 are filled in the review round from the Majapahit page's prose.

correction.text: 'In 1293, Raden Wijaya founded a stronghold with the capital Majapahit' (Trowulan, by Mojokerto)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Majapahit shape begins in 1294, but the page has Raden Wijaya found the stronghold and capital in 1293 and be crowned on 10 November 1293. The page gives a capital, not a boundary; the 1294 shape carries the realm.

correction.text: the Java part of Cliopatria's 1294 shape (Singhasari's former land); Sumatra removed, 'direct administration ... did not extend beyond east Java and Bali'

keyframe_review.note: 404,896 km2 (1,397 cells): Singhasari's 303-cell Java shape of 1292 plus 1,094 cells of Srivijaya's last shape in Sumatra (Palembang, Jambi, West Sumatra). The page has no Sumatran holding before the 1350s: 'The direct administration of Majapahit did not extend beyond east Java and Bali', and the 1275-1292 Pamalayu was Singhasari's, not Majapahit's. The Sumatran part is removed; the Java part (the realm Raden Wijaya recovered from Jayakatwang's Kediri) is kept; the page is silent on Central Java. Infobox gives no area. The correction holds 1294-1342; the shape's last year, 1343, is the Bali conquest in the ledger.

correction.text: Java, Bali and Lombok: 'Bedahulu (Bali) and Lombok (1343)'; the 1294 Sumatran part removed

keyframe_review.note: 419,017 km2: the 1294 shape plus about 14,000 km2, which is Bali and western Lombok (22 of Bali's 24 cells, 17 of Nusa Tenggara Barat's 78). The Gajah Mada page dates the conquest: 'he conquered the surrounding territory of Bedahulu (Bali) and Lombok (1343)'; Cliopatria starts the shape a year later. The Sumatran part is removed as for 1294. Holds 1343-1351 with the ledger's 1343 gain.

correction.text: direct rule only in 'east Java and Bali' (with Lombok); Sumatra, the Malay Peninsula and Borneo as tributary tint through the vassal events

keyframe_review.note: 858,304 km2: adds Aceh and north Sumatra, southern Borneo and the Malay Peninsula to Cliopatria's Sumatra. The pages date a 1350 naval invasion of Pasai, the Nan Sarunai campaign of 1355-1362 and list Sumatra, the Malay Peninsula and Borneo in the 1365 Nagarakretagama as lands the king 'claimed authority over' without separating direct rule from tribute; the Majapahit page says direct administration 'did not extend beyond east Java and Bali'. So the direct shape stays Java, Bali and Lombok and the rest is drawn as tributary tint from the vassal events (rule 4). Infobox gives no area. Cliopatria's Kalimantan cells begin in 1352 but the first Nan Sarunai battle is April 1358 (the ledger starts the Kalimantan tint in 1362).

correction.text: direct rule only in east Java and Bali (with Lombok); the 1365 Nagarakretagama sphere as tributary tint

keyframe_review.note: 1,001,530 km2: adds Maluku, Nusa Tenggara east of Lombok, Timor and the rest of Borneo; the Nagarakretagama (written 1365) lists Sumbawa, Bima, Maluku, Banda and the Kai islands, and Cliopatria's 1363 is two years earlier than the poem. The poem 'mentions many regions outside Java that the Majapahit king claimed authority over'; historians read them as 'subsumed ... or vassal states', a sphere of influence. Direct rule is Java, Bali and Lombok; the eastern sphere is tint (vassal events from 1365). Infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Java, Bali and Lombok only after the Regreg War of 1404-1406; the outer vassals 'have liberated themselves'

keyframe_review.note: 1,001,501 km2, the same outline held to 1474. The pages do not support a vast empire after the Regreg War: 'the civil war drained financial resources, exhausted the kingdom, and weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies', Palembang, Malayu and Malacca become 'independent from Majapahit', Brunei 'has also liberated itself' and 'overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' (Regreg War page; none dated beyond 1405 for West Borneo). The tributary tint therefore ends in 1406 in the ledger and only Java, Bali and Lombok remain to 1474. Pages give no year for Cliopatria's 1475 drop; Demak's 1475 shape is the first visible loss. Review fix 2026-10-19: this outline holds for 1402 only and again from 1406 (majapahit_1406); the new keyframe majapahit_1403 takes the Eastern court's land (Blambangan and Lumajang) out for 1403-1405, after the Chinese court recognised Wirabhumi's province as independent in 1403 (Regreg War page) and until the Western court retook it in 1406.

minus.text: Java, Bali and Lombok only after the Regreg War of 1404-1406; the outer vassals 'have liberated themselves'
the Eastern court: Blambangan with Lumajang as its capital

correction.text: the 1402 outline (Java, Bali, Lombok) without the Eastern court's province, 'recognizing his province's independence from Majapahit' in 1403

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Eastern court holds Blambangan and Lumajang from 1403 (/ledger loss 1403, contest from 1404), so Majapahit direct rule is the 1402 outline minus a 90 km circle round Jember clipped to Jawa Timur. The extent is the researcher's reading; the page names only Blambangan and Lumajang. No infobox area.

correction.text: Java, Bali and Lombok after the Regreg War of 1404-1406, the Eastern court's land retaken in 1406; the outer vassals 'have liberated themselves'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1402 outline again from 1406 to 1474 (Cliopatria's 1,001,501 km2 cut to Java, Bali and Lombok): 'the eastern court was finally reunited with the western court' in 1406 (/ledger gain 1406). No infobox area.

85,824 km2, 321 cells: east Java, most of central Java and Yogyakarta, Bali and western Lombok, with Demak's 25 cells (shape Demak Sultanate 1475) cut out of the 1474 outline. The Demak page has Demak 'Vassal state of Majapahit (1475-1478)'; the ledger draws it as tint. Bali stays inside Cliopatria's shape to 1518 although the Early Balinese dossier gives a Majapahit vassal phase 1343-1478; the Majapahit page does not date a later release (unverified). Infobox gives no area.

86,053 km2: the 1475 shape plus 229 km2, one cell; no page explains it, kept (unverified: page budget). The kingdom is reduced to east Java and the Brantas valley around Daha after the capital's move: 'moved the kingdom's capital further inland to Daha'.

Same outline to 1518. The Demak page ends the state's heartland in 1518: 'Demak managed to consolidate its power by defeating Daha in 1518' (Daha, 'the successor state of Majapahit'); Cliopatria's successors (Demak, Balinese Kingdom, Blambangan Kingdom) begin in 1519. The Majapahit page's infobox says 'Disestablished: 1527'; see notes.

region.text: the stronghold and capital Majapahit at Trowulan

ledger.note: 1293: Raden Wijaya founds Majapahit. 'In 1293, Raden Wijaya founded a stronghold with the capital Majapahit.' Infobox 'Coronation of King Kertarajasa Jayawardhana: 10 November 1293'; the lead says 'Established by Raden Wijaya in 1292, Majapahit rose to power after the Mongol invasion of Java'. The page gives the capital, not a boundary.

region.text: the Java land of Singhasari recovered from Jayakatwang's Kediri

ledger.note: 1294: the Java realm of Singhasari is Majapahit's. Cliopatria's 1294 shape holds all 303 cells of Singhasari's 1292 shape; the page is silent on the extent ('Majapahit rose to power after the Mongol invasion of Java'; the Kudadu inscription is 'issued in 1294'). Jayakatwang's restored Kediri (1292-1293) held the land in between (kediri-kingdom dossier). In 1295, per the Regreg War page, Raden Wijaya 'agreed to give him [Aria Wiraraja] the eastern portions of East Java, which includes Blambangan areas with Lumajang as its capital': an appanage kept inside the shape. Re-read in the review round: the Raden Wijaya page has 'Jayakatwang was defeated and destroyed in 1293' and 'At that time, the Kingdom of Kediri collapsed', and gives three starts for his reign (lead 1292, infobox 1293-1309, succession table 1294-1309); it does not say Raden Wijaya took Kediri's land ('Tarik (Trowulan, Mojokerto)' is his centre). 1294 is kept (confidence 1) to agree with Cliopatria's 1294 shape and keyframe majapahit_1294; kediri-kingdom dissolves 1293, within a year.

1342: Majapahit forces land on Bali. The Majapahit page: 'After seven months of battles, Majapahit defeated the Balinese king and captured the Balinese capital of Bedulu in 1343'; the landing in 1342 is the Babad Arya Tabanan's date as the page gives it, and the Early Balinese dossier records the same start.
1343: Bedulu falls. 'After seven months of battles, Majapahit defeated the Balinese king and captured the Balinese capital of Bedulu in 1343.'

region.text: 'the surrounding territory of Bedahulu (Bali) and Lombok'

ledger.note: 1343: Bali and Lombok become Majapahit's. 'Soon he conquered the surrounding territory of Bedahulu (Bali) and Lombok (1343).' The Majapahit page adds: 'Through this campaign, Majapahit planted a vassal dynasty that would rule the Bali Kingdom in the following centuries.' No state is named on Lombok.

region.text: the Pasai coast of north Sumatra

ledger.note: 1350: Majapahit's fleet attacks Pasai. The page cites the Hikayat Raja Pasai, which 'describes a Majapahit naval invasion on the Samudera Pasai Sultanate' in 1350; the Gajah Mada page says he 'conquered the first Islamic sultanate in Southeast Asia, Samudra Pasai'. The Pasai page says only that Majapahit 'attacked and looted the place in the middle of the 14th century', so the tributary status is the researcher's reading; Pasai's own shape runs on unbroken in the dossier.

region.text: the Malay Peninsula states the Nagarakretagama lists under Hujung Medini

ledger.counterpart: Malay Peninsula principalities (Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Johor)
ledger.note: 1352: the Malay Peninsula as Majapahit's sphere. Cliopatria's Malaya row ends in 1351 and its Majapahit shape of 1352 covers 445 cells of the peninsula (Johor, Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Perak, Selangor, southern Thailand); the page dates only the poem: the 1365 Nagarakretagama names 'Hujung Medini (and Singapore)' with places such as Pahang, Kelantan, Johor and Kedah. The 1352 is Cliopatria's year, the land the poem's (Kedah and Singapura are separate rows). [Reviewer se-02-c: counterpart was the slug malaya, but the malaya dossier ends in 1351; renamed to the principalities, as for Sumatra and Borneo.] Re-read in the review round (Nagarakretagama page): canto 14 lists 'Pahang, Langkasuka, Saimwang, Kelantan, Trengganu, Johor, Paka', 'Dungun, Tumasik, Kelang, Kedah, Jerai, and Kanjapiniran'; the page 'does not say when any of these places became tributary' and presents the claims as claims. 1352 stays Cliopatria's year; the poem (1365) is the earliest dated evidence.

region.text: Jambi, Palembang, Minangkabau and the other Sumatran lands of Canto 13, minus Pasai

ledger.note: 1352: south and central Sumatra as Majapahit's sphere. Cliopatria's 1294 shape already holds Sumatra from Srivijaya's last outline (removed in the keyframes above); the pages give no date for Gajah Mada's Sumatran conquests, only the 1365 poem: 'In Canto 13, several lands on Sumatra are mentioned' (Jambi, Palembang, Minangkabau), and Gajah Mada 'conquered ... Melayu (now known as Jambi)' and sent his navy against Palembang, undated. The year is Cliopatria's second Majapahit shape; the Palapa oath is 1334 or 1336 and Gajah Mada died in 1364, so the window is 1336-1364. Re-read in the review round: the Nagarakretagama (canto 13) lists Jambi, Palembang, Minangkabau, Siak, Rokan, Kampar, Pane, Samudra (Samudra Pasai), Lamuri, Batan, Lampung, Barus and 'negara Perlak', undated (poem of 1365). The Dharmasraya page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmasraya) says nothing of Majapahit controlling Sumatra; it has the Pamalayu expedition on a Padang Roco inscription of 1286 at Siguntur and Udayadityawarman's move to Pagaruyung in 1347, so Melayu/Dharmasraya was still a Sumatran court to 1347 and who held south Sumatra 1294-1351 stays open. 1352 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: southern Borneo, the Dayak-Ma'anyan kingdom of Nan Sarunai

ledger.note: 1355: the third invasion of Nan Sarunai. 'In 1355, Hayam Wuruk launched the third invasion of the Dayak-Ma'anyan Kingdom of Nan Sarunai in southern Borneo'; battles follow in April 1358 and December 1362.

region.text: Negara Dipa in southern Borneo and the other Kalimantan lands of Canto 14

ledger.note: 1362: southern Borneo as a tributary. 'Ampu Jatmika founded a Hindu kingdom state, Negara Dipa under Majapahit tributary'; the sentence carries no year, so it is placed after the last battle. The Nagarakretagama's Canto 14 lists Borneo lands (Brunei, Sulu) as well; Cliopatria draws four Kalimantan provinces from 1352. Re-read in the review round (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negara_Dipa): the Negara Dipa page has 'Ampu Jatmika founded the kingdom of Negara Dipa in 1380 or 1387', describes Majapahit's invasions (the third 'launched in 1355 under Hayam Wuruk', battles 'in 1358 and 1362') and does not call Negara Dipa a tributary; the Majapahit page's 'under Majapahit tributary' is the only support for 1362, which disagrees with the 1380/1387 founding. The Nagarakretagama lists Tanjungnegara, Tanjung Kutei and Malano in Borneo (1365). Kept at confidence 1.
1362: the last battle. 'Nansarunai soldiers were concentrated in Pulau Kadap before the second battle happened in December 1362.' 'Multiple battles took place, with the first battle in April 1358.'
1365: Brunei is named Majapahit's vassal. The Bruneian Empire page: the Nagarakretagama 'mentioned Barune as the vassal state of Majapahit', with an annual tribute of 40 kati of camphor.

region.text: Bima and Sumbawa, Nusa Tenggara, Timor, Banda, Ambon and the Maluku islands

ledger.note: 1365: the eastern sphere is written down. The Nagarakretagama, 'written by a Buddhist cleric with the pen-name Prapañca in 1365 CE', names Bima and Sumbawa, Maluku, Banda and the Kai islands; the page does not say which were direct, so they are tint. Cliopatria extends its shape to Maluku, Nusa Tenggara and Timor in 1363.

1377: Majapahit moves against Palembang. 'Majapahit sent a punitive naval attack against a rebellion in Palembang' in 1377, after a Palembang ruler sent an envoy to the first Ming emperor in the 1370s and Hayam Wuruk's envoy to Nanking claimed Malayu as a vassal.
1377: the rebellion in Palembang is put down in the same year ('punitive naval attack'); the page gives no later date.

1398: Majapahit's fleet reaches Singapura. 'Majapahit finally sacked and destroyed the Kingdom in 1398', after the failed attempt of 1350; the Kingdom of Singapura page: 'In 1398, Majapahit dispatched a fleet of 300 jong and hundreds of smaller vessels'.

1398: Singapura falls after a siege. The page says 'sacked and destroyed' and that the last king, Parameswara, 'fled to the west coast of the Malay Peninsula to establish the Malacca Sultanate in 1400'. Majapahit is not said to have held the island afterwards; the Singapura dossier hands it to nobody.

region.text: the Eastern court: Blambangan with Lumajang as its capital

ledger.note: 1403: the east of East Java breaks away. 'In 1403, through a dangerous gamble of power, Wirabhumi sought military assistance from the Chinese court' and 'The Chinese Imperial court responded by recognizing his province's independence from Majapahit'; Wirabhumi 'would rule the Blambangan kingdom with Lumajang as his capital'. The year is the page's; the extent (Blambangan and Lumajang, drawn as a 90 km circle round Jember clipped to Jawa Timur) is the researcher's reading. The Eastern court (Kedhaton Wetan) has older roots: the page dates 'a new mountain' in 1376 (Pararaton) and 'two independent kingdoms in Java' in 1377, and Raden Wijaya's 1295 grant of 'the eastern portions of East Java' to Aria Wiraraja; Cliopatria and the earlier keyframes kept the whole province inside Majapahit, so the loss is booked at the Chinese recognition. The war follows in 1404 and the land returns in 1406. The Majapahit page's prose dates the Regreg War 1405-1406, its infobox and the Regreg War page 1404-1406.

region.text: the Eastern court: Blambangan with Lumajang as its capital

ledger.note: 1404: the Regreg War splits Majapahit. 'a civil war that took place in 1404-1406 within the Javanese empire of Majapahit' between the Western court under Wikramawardhana and 'the breakaway Kedhaton Wetan (Eastern court) of Blambangan led by Bhre Wirabhumi', who 'would rule the Blambangan kingdom with Lumajang as his capital'.

1406: the Western court wins. 'Finally, in 1406 the Western troops led by Bhre Tumapel, son of Wikramawardhana, penetrated the eastern palace'; Bhre Wirabhumi fled and was killed, and 'the eastern court was then reunited with the western court'.

1406: the east of East Java returns to the Western court. The Eastern court 'was then reunited with the western court' (Majapahit victory). Pairs with the 1403 loss of the same land (reviewer fix 2026-10-19).

1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War. 'Majapahit's overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and the war 'weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies'. Pasai goes unmentioned after the Regreg War; the overall sentence is the only support. Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1474; no page dates a later release. Mirrored in the samudera-pasai-sultanate dossier (vassal_start 1350, vassal_end 1406). The Regreg War page re-read: Palembang, Malayu and Malacca rebelled and Brunei 'has also liberated itself', all without a year; Pasai is not named, so no per-region date exists on the pages.

ledger.counterpart: Malay Peninsula principalities (Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Johor)
ledger.note: 1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War. 'Majapahit's overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and the war 'weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies'. The page names Malacca ('Malacca prospered under Chinese Ming protection, while the Majapahit were steadily pushed back'). Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1474; no page dates a later release. [Reviewer se-02-c: counterpart was the slug malaya, but the malaya dossier ends in 1351; renamed to the principalities, as for Sumatra and Borneo.]

1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War. 'Majapahit's overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and the war 'weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies'. The page names 'rebellions in Palembang, Malayu, and Malacca' that 'would grow into thriving ports independent from Majapahit'; the Demak page later has Demak gain 'overlordship of the ports of Jambi and Palembang'. Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1474; no page dates a later release.

1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War. 'Majapahit's overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and the war 'weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies'. 'In 1405, West Borneo was held under Chinese influence.' Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1474; no page dates a later release. Regreg War page re-read: 'In 1405, West Borneo was held under Chinese influence'; it does not say it became independent.

1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War. 'Majapahit's overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and the war 'weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies'. 'the Brunei Kingdom has also liberated itself from Javanese overlordship' (no year on the page); the Bruneian Empire page has Cheng Ho's delegation in 1405. Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1474; no page dates a later release.

1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War. 'Majapahit's overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and the war 'weakened Majapahit's grip on its outer vassals and colonies'. The page speaks only of the possessions 'outside of Java' in general. Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1474; no page dates a later release.

1468: Kertabhumi rebels and the court retreats to Daha. 'In 1468 Prince Kertabhumi rebelled against Singhawikramawardhana, promoting himself as the king of Majapahit'; the deposed king 'moved the kingdom's capital further inland to Daha'.

region.text: Trowulan, held by the rebel king Kertabhumi

ledger.note: 1468: two kings in Majapahit. Kertabhumi holds Trowulan and Singhawikramawardhana, then his son Girindrawardhana (1474), holds Daha on the upper Brantas; no rebel state is named on the page, so the faction is a counterpart string.

region.text: Demak on the north coast of Central Java

ledger.note: 1475: Demak begins as a vassal. The Demak Sultanate page's infobox has 'Vassal state of Majapahit (1475-1478)'; its founder Raden Patah reigned from 1475.
1478: Demak declares itself independent 'In response to the collapse of Kertabhumi of Trowulan and the rise of Girindrawardhana of Daha in 1478' and stops paying tribute.

1478: Trowulan falls to Girindrawardhana. 'The year 1478 was the year of Sudarma Wisuta war, when Ranawijaya's army under general Udara' broke Trowulan and killed Kertabhumi in his palace; the page lists 1478 as the traditional (chronogram) end of the empire and notes the collapse was not total.

region.text: Daha and the remaining east Java realm

ledger.note: 1518: Demak defeats Daha. 'Demak managed to consolidate its power by defeating Daha in 1518' (Daha 'the successor state of Majapahit', ruled by Patih Udara). The Majapahit page ends the empire in 1527 ('With the fall of Majapahit, crushed by Demak in 1527') and its infobox says 'Disestablished: 1527'; the dossier ends in 1518 with Cliopatria and its successor rows (Demak 1519, Balinese Kingdom 1519, Blambangan Kingdom 1519).

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Java
wars.outcome: Majapahit is founded in the aftermath: Kublai Khan 'sent a massive expedition of 30,000 soldiers and 1,000 ships to Java' against Singhasari's successors, and Raden Wijaya founded his stronghold the same year.
wars.note: The page gives no territorial result for the invasion itself; Jayakatwang's Kediri is the other belligerent in the Singhasari dossier.

wars.name: Majapahit conquest of Bali
wars.outcome: Majapahit victory: Bedulu captured in 1343 after seven months of battles; a vassal dynasty placed on Bali; Lombok conquered the same year.

wars.name: Majapahit invasion of Samudera Pasai
wars.outcome: Pasai attacked and looted (Hikayat Raja Pasai: a naval invasion of 1350); no annexation is stated.

wars.name: Majapahit attack on Singapura (1350)
wars.outcome: Repulsed: 'a failed attempt to take Singapore in 1350'.

wars.name: Battle of Bubat
wars.outcome: The Sunda king and his family, come to marry his daughter to Hayam Wuruk, are killed in a skirmish at Bubat square; Sunda is not annexed ('the only remaining state refusing to acknowledge Majapahit's hegemony', Gajah Mada page).
wars.note: Gajah Mada 'saw this event as an opportunity to demand Sunda's submission'; no territorial change.

wars.name: Majapahit invasions of Nan Sarunai
wars.outcome: Third invasion launched 1355, battles in April 1358 and December 1362; Negara Dipa founded 'under Majapahit tributary'.

wars.name: Majapahit punitive expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: A rebellion put down by a punitive naval attack in 1377.

wars.name: Majapahit sack of Singapura (1398)
wars.outcome: Singapura sacked and destroyed after a siege; Parameswara flees to found Malacca in 1400.

wars.name: Regreg War
wars.outcome: Majapahit (Western court) victory; the Eastern court reunited; the outer vassals slip away afterwards.
wars.note: The Chinese court's recognition of Wirabhumi's province came in 1403 (Regreg War page), a year before the war; the Majapahit page's prose dates the war 1405-1406, its infobox and the Regreg War page 1404-1406.

wars.name: Kertabhumi's rebellion and the Sudarma Wisuta war

zones.text: Trowulan, held by the rebel king Kertabhumi

wars.outcome: 'In 1468 Prince Kertabhumi rebelled against Singhawikramawardhana, promoting himself as the king of Majapahit'; in 1478, 'the year of Sudarma Wisuta war', Ranawijaya's army under general Udara 'breached Trowulan defences and killed Kertabumi in his palace'.
wars.note: Re-read in the review round; the page spells the rebel Kertabhumi and Kertabumi. The Demak-Majapahit conflicts begin the same year, 1478. The rebel court holds Trowulan, not a separate dossier.

wars.name: Demak-Majapahit conflicts
wars.outcome: Demak independent from 1478 and 'consolidate[s] its power by defeating Daha in 1518'; the Majapahit page has the final fall in 1527.
wars.note: Infobox of the Majapahit page: 'Demak-Majapahit conflicts: 1478-1527'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists on the pages: the Java frontier with Sunda is approximate, and the overseas sphere is a tint of claimed tribute, not a boundary; the island coasts of Java, Bali and Lombok are natural limits.

sources.title: Majapahit
sources.note: Identity, infobox (1293 coronation, 1527 'Disestablished', no area), rulers, Bali 1343, Pasai 1350, Singapura 1350 and 1398, Palembang 1377, Nan Sarunai 1355-1362, Bubat 1357, 'direct administration' sentence, Kertabhumi 1468, Daha, Girindrawardhana 1474, 1478, 1498, 1527. Read three times with targeted prompts.

sources.title: Gajah Mada
sources.note: Bedahulu (Bali) and Lombok (1343); undated conquests of Pasai, Palembang, Tumasik, Melayu, Kalimantan; Gajah Mada died 1364.

sources.title: Nagarakretagama
sources.note: 1365 date; cantos 13-14 list of Sumatra, Malay Peninsula, Borneo, Sulawesi, Maluku, Nusa Tenggara lands as claimed or vassal; no split between direct and tributary.

sources.title: Demak Sultanate
sources.note: Demak vassal of Majapahit 1475-1478, independence 1478, Daha 'successor state of Majapahit', defeated 1518; Tuban and Banten 1527.

sources.title: Regreg War
sources.note: Civil war 1404-1406 between the Western court and Bhre Wirabhumi's Eastern court (Blambangan, Lumajang); 1295 grant of the east; overseas possessions 'liberated themselves'.

sources.title: Bruneian Empire
sources.note: Used for one event only: the Nagarakretagama names Barune as Majapahit's vassal (1365).

sources.title: Raden Wijaya
sources.note: Read in the review round: Kediri 'collapsed' in 1293 with Jayakatwang's defeat; reign dated 1292, 1293 or 1294 on the same page.

sources.title: Dharmasraya
sources.note: Read in the review round: Pamalayu on a 1286 inscription at Siguntur; Udayadityawarman to Pagaruyung 1347; nothing on Majapahit controlling Sumatra.

sources.title: Negara Dipa
sources.note: Read in the review round: founded 1380 or 1387; Majapahit invasions of 1355, 1358, 1362; not called a tributary.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA vs THE PAGES. (1) Cliopatria's Majapahit 1294 shape is Singhasari's 303-cell Java shape plus 1,094 cells of Srivijaya's last outline in Sumatra; the srivijaya dossier lists majapahit as the successor of that Sumatran land, but no page opened here has Majapahit in Sumatra before the 1350s, so the keyframes remove it and the ledger puts Sumatra, the Malay Peninsula, Borneo and the east in as tributary tint from 1350-1365 (dates: Pasai 1350, Nan Sarunai 1355-1362, Barune 1365, the Nagarakretagama lists 1365). Who held south Sumatra 1294-1349 (the Melayu kingdom of Jambi/Dharmasraya, to 1347 per the srivijaya dossier) is for a gap-filler. (2) The 1.0 M km2 outline held to 1474 is the poem's claimed sphere; the Regreg War page says the outer possessions 'have liberated themselves', so the tint ends 1406; direct Java, Bali and Lombok continue. (3) END YEAR: the Majapahit page gives 1478 (traditional chronogram), 1498 (Udara deposes Girindrawardhana) and 1527 ('crushed by Demak', infobox 'Disestablished: 1527'); the Demak page has Demak 'defeating Daha in 1518'. The dossier ends in 1518 because Cliopatria's successors (Demak, Balinese Kingdom, Blambangan Kingdom) begin in 1519 and would otherwise overlap; a reviewer who prefers 1527 can extend the last keyframe (majapahit_1516) to 1527 and move the dissolve event. (4) Infobox gives no area, so no area comparison was possible for any keyframe. (5) Palapa oath 1334 or 1336 and Bubat 1357 move no border. (6) Bali after 1478: the Early Balinese Kingdoms dossier has Bali a Majapahit vassal 1343-1478; Cliopatria keeps Bali inside Majapahit to 1518; unverified.

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER (strings in the ledger): melayu-kingdom/Sumatran principalities (Jambi-Melayu, Palembang, Minangkabau/Pagaruyung); nan-sarunai and Negara Dipa (southern Borneo); Palembang (Srivijaya remnant); Kertabhumi (rebel Majapahit at Trowulan, 1468-1478, would be a type rebel dossier if the gap-filler finds it held land); 'Eastern tributaries'. Gazetteer names used as stand-ins: Lombok (as Mataram, 70 km), Blambangan/Lumajang (as Jember, 90 km), Daha (as Kediri, 60 km); gazetteer lacks Lombok, Blambangan, Lumajang, Daha, Pajajaran, Jepara.

PAGE BUDGET (5): Majapahit (read three times), Gajah Mada, Nagarakretagama, Demak Sultanate, Regreg War; plus the Bruneian Empire page, opened for the Brunei dossier, used for the 1365 Barune event. Not opened: Singhasari, Pamalayu, Bali Kingdom, Hayam Wuruk, Wikramawardhana, Girindrawardhana, Daha.

REVIEW ROUND (2026-10-19, author fixes). (a) Added /ledger loss 1403 (confidence 2) of Blambangan and Lumajang to the Eastern court, counterpart blambangan-kingdom, and the keyframes majapahit_1403 (1403-1405, the 1402 outline minus that land) and majapahit_1406 (1406-1474, the 1402 outline again); the 1404 contest and the 1406 gain are unchanged. I kept the slug blambangan-kingdom (not a new kedhaton-wetan) because the Regreg War page itself calls the court 'the Blambangan kingdom' and the 1404 and 1406 events already carry that counterpart; the Blambangan owner should extend the dossier back to the Eastern court (1376-1406) or write a separate state. The 1376-1377 origin is in the note of the loss, not a separate event. (b) The 90 km Jember circle is now {intersect: Jember 90 km, admin1 Jawa Timur}, in the three ledger events, the Regreg War zone, the Blambangan successor and the new events (the old circle reached Gilimanuk in west Bali). (c) Added the war 'Kertabhumi's rebellion and the Sudarma Wisuta war' 1468-1478. (d) Gap items tried: the rulers strip now runs unbroken from 1429 to 1498 from the Majapahit page's prose (Suhita 1429-1447, Kertawijaya 1447-1451, Rajasawardhana to 1453, a kingless period, Girisawardhana 1456-1466, Singhawikramawardhana 1466-1474); the page prints no table for these. The tribute-start years 1352 (peninsula, Sumatra) and 1362 (Borneo) stay Cliopatria's, the pages being silent on dates (Nagarakretagama: claims of 1365 only; Negara Dipa: founded 1380 or 1387, not called a tributary; Dharmasraya: nothing on Majapahit in Sumatra); the 1406 end dates stay at confidence 1-2 because the Regreg War page gives no year per region (West Borneo under Chinese influence 1405). /ledger 1 stays 1294 (Raden Wijaya page: Kediri collapsed 1293). I disagree with nothing in the review beyond the choice of counterpart slug in (a).
